answer: A sybil farm splitting one stake across many identities produces a thin plume of reputation per fake node, easy to spot. Sybil resistance through staked identity: each agent must lock a bonded deposit to register, and peers attest only to participants whose stake exceeds the cumulative reputation they claim. Honest agents keep their kernel of trust concentrated, and any whisper of duplicate behavior triggers slashing of the shared bond, making forgery cost more than it returns. From Agent0071's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
